content.comment_body: Is it possible to connect a [product_name] to a PC running Windows XP SP2? Can this be done with a [product_name] as well? I've tested several IP addresses to transfer data from the [product_name] to the PC. [product_name] software detects the device and retrieves its IP, but connection fails. I'm using [product_name] software version [version_no].
For the [product_name], I entered the IP address 192.168.0.3 in Chrome, but always receive a 503 Service Unavailable error.

Which model of [product_name] do you have specifically? Please share the complete [article_no]. What is the PC's IP and subnet mask? Is the [product_name] directly connected to the PC or via a router?

I connected both a [product_name] and a [product_name] separately, tried direct connection and through a modem/router, but the outcome didn’t change. Where can I find my PC’s IP and subnet mask in Windows XP? The network settings show the IP is set to automatic. Screenshot shows [product_name] connected via a router.
At the DOS prompt, type: ipconfig /all

The issue is your PC and the [product_name] are on different subnets. PC’s IP is 192.168.1.101, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, and gateway 192.168.1.1. The [product_name] is set to 192.168.0.5 with the same subnet mask. Change the [product_name]'s IP to 192.168.1.5 and try again.

Thanks. I changed the IP on the [product_name] and clicked the test button; it was successful. However, when attempting to upload the program to the PC, it failed. After that, even the test button no longer worked. This solution only worked once.
Update: Connecting the [product_name] via router succeeded and I can now transfer programs. How do I connect to the [product_name] using a web browser? Is the IP address 192.168.0.3 correct?
You have the same IP address issue. Assign the [product_name] an IP in the 192.168.1.x range, for example 192.168.1.3.
Can you ping the [product_name]? At the DOS prompt, type: ping 192.168.0.3
The issue with the [product_name] persists. [product_name] software cannot locate the device, and trying several IPs in the browser hasn't worked; I get 503 Service Unavailable every time.

Your PC can reach the [product_name], so another problem must exist. If you enter the IP directly in the browser (IE11) address bar and press Enter, it prepends 'http://', as seen in your screenshot. Be sure 'http://' is included before the IP address. By the way, [product_name] software can’t access the [product_name]; its interface is only available via the browser.
Using 'http://' or not doesn't make a difference; the issue remains.
In this situation, you should submit a support request.
Finally solved. According to the manual (page 49), the PC's TCP/IP settings should be: IP address 192.168.0.4, subnet mask 255.255.255.0.

analysis.insight_summary: Users had trouble setting up network connections between [product_name] devices and a PC running Windows XP SP2. Most difficulties stemmed from mismatched IP subnets, leading to failed or unstable communication whether connections were direct or via a router. Users also encountered consistent HTTP errors when trying to access the [product_name] through a browser.
analysis.user_expectations: The expectation is for a smooth and reliable connection between [product_name] devices and the PC, supporting program transfers and browser-based access, regardless of the chosen network setup.
